Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: separate upgrade PARTS for an existing top-down 2D fictional helicopter game sprite, level 2 only, on genuine transparency. Inputs: Image 1 is the APPROVED scout body with seven banking frames (nose RIGHT, first frame neutral) — preserve its olive grey paint, angular mechanical style, no aircraft redesign. Images 2–4 are original game's machine-gun mech body levels 8/9/10, for restrained metal shading and independently attached plate construction only; do not copy their silhouette. Image 5 contains the approved scout gun on the left and missile housing on the right, separated by a transparent gap; these two small parts are the exact edit targets.
Produce exactly THREE SEPARATED, orthographic top-view sprite parts arranged in one horizontal row, generous transparent gutters, NO text/no labels/no background/no ground shadow:
LEFT: a small two-shoulder engine-cover assembly to fit ONLY inside the existing scout center hull, nose to the RIGHT. Two thin independent olive-grey supporting armor plates with one short exposed mechanical bridge and the existing central rotor opening left transparent. Short bright metal corners and dark seams, one clear upper surface per plate. Not a complete fuselage, no nose, tail, wings, rotor, antenna, or new decoration. Logical footprint at final game size about 22x18 pixels, readable few large forms.
CENTER: edit current scout machine-gun housing, keeping barrel number, RIGHT-pointing muzzle and the length/width ratio of its 14x7 logical pixel sprite EXACTLY; add only a short rear protective hood and exposed attachment. No enlarged barrel or extra guns.
RIGHT: edit current scout missile pod 13x8 proportions EXACTLY, keeping tube count/muzzle and RIGHT direction; add a short mechanical retaining band at the rear. No added tubes.
All parts share identical pixel density and neutral top-down camera. Preserve low-saturation olive grey, small ivory edge highlights, dark metal crevices. The structure must change, not just recoloring/scratches. No orange/neon/new color patches, rounded shiny 3D rendering, thick outlines, or random micro-noise. These are separate modular replacement parts, NOT a complete helicopter.
